learning_outcomes.text: Understand what a project is and the most important project management systems.
Know the knowledge areas to consider for proper project management (integration, time, cost, quality, human resources, communication, and risks).
Use computer tools to support project management.

syllabus_topics: Motivation for the project, academic project vs. real projects
State of the art, bibliographic references and plagiarism
How to correctly perform a state of the art
How to define and describe the objectives of a Project
How to define activities and estimate their duration
Management of material and human resources of a Project
How to estimate a budget and control expenses
How to establish a good communication plan
Identify risks and opportunities of a Project
Analysis of ethical behavior in the professional environment: Risks and challenges

assessment_methods.method: Intermediate follow-up meeting and report on group work (Projects part)
Final submission of group work and oral presentation (Projects part)
Evaluation of theoretical content seen in Deontology classes

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of 85% for Projects and 15% for Deontology. The Projects part consists of a 30% intermediate report and a 70% final group work with an oral presentation. The Deontology part consists of 50% active participation and 50% evaluation of theoretical content. For the extraordinary call, students must re-elaborate only the suspended part; for Projects, this means correcting the submitted project, and for Deontology, it involves developing and analyzing an ethical conflict case, without considering class attendance.
